name: Realistic Finish + Widened Skill Spread
notes: Post-Sonoma rebuild. Two coupled changes fix the v3.1 knife-edge: (1) a proportional finish -- the winner is drawn with probability proportional to race-long pace ^ decisiveness, instead of whoever led the final lap; (2) widened skill weights (~8x v3.1) so drivers span a real ~25-30% strength range. Together these let a clear favorite emerge from SKILL at a gentle setting, while form and tilt features move the board proportionately instead of exploding. Consequence: on a road course the road master is favored (SVG over Larson) -- which is what actually happened at Sonoma.
calibration_note: Favorite ~16% over a real chase pack; oval specialists correctly low; a +3% form nudge moves a driver ~5 points (was +77 under v3.1's deterministic finish). Tilt features can now be enabled safely, but learning (form) is the preferred way to encode what actually happens.

from_v3_1: finish.method: proportional (was implicit final-lap argmax) -- smooth response to inputs
finish.decisiveness: 10 -- sharpness of the favorite, replaces the old variance knife-edge
skill weights scaled ~8x so the field spans a real ~25-30% pace range; a clear favorite now comes from skill, not from a near-deterministic finish
form/tilt now move win share proportionately (a +3% form bump = ~+5 points, was ~+77)
